title: TypeScript emitter for polymorphic response contracts + Zod/JSON-Schema bridge for streaming outputs
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: TypeScript SDK users need first-class ergonomics for model responses that can be polymorphic (discriminated unions, variants) when streaming tokens. Currently we emit broad 'any' or simple unions that break type safety for progressive parsers and streaming partial payloads. Goal: implement a code-emitter in the tsc pipeline that produces robust TypeScript types for polymorphic response contracts, plus runtime validators/guards generated for Zod and JSON-Schema. The emitter must support progressive/streaming parsing: allow partial chunk validation, progressive hydration of discriminators, and graceful fallback for incomplete streams. Deliverables: 1) emitter that generates union types with stable discriminators and optional progressive parsers; 2) zod schemas alongside types (zodify option) and JSON-Schema artifacts for downstream tooling; 3) streaming helpers that let SDK consumers progressively decode chunks and receive strongly-typed partials; 4) examples and migration guide for existing users.
acceptance_criteria: Generated .d.ts files include discriminated union types with stable 'variant' discriminator and per-variant payload types
Emitter can produce companion zod schemas that pass round-trip validation against sample model outputs
JSON-Schema artifacts produced for CI-based contract checks and server-side validation
Streaming parser exposes a decodeIncremental(streamChunk) API that returns typed Partial<T> and an onComplete typed T for consumers
Benchmarks show <5% token throughput regression for codegen step and <10ms added latency for incremental parse on 2kB chunks
Integration test with runtime streaming example app (examples/streaming-playground.ts) demonstrates progressive hydration across three real model variants
test_plan: Unit tests for emitter: fixture-driven asserts comparing generated types/schemas to goldens. End-to-end tests: run tsc build on sample contracts, run streaming-playground to ingest recorded streaming traces, assert final hydrated object matches expected variant. Contract CI job validates produced JSON-Schema against sample payloads. Fuzz streaming parser with truncated chunks to verify graceful partials and reassembly.
notes: 2026-01-22: Kickoff meeting — agreed on 'variant' as the default discriminator key instead of 'type' to avoid collision with model-generated 'type' fields. Action: update design doc.

2026-01-29: Prototype emitter that emits tagged unions using 'variant' + per-variant interfaces. Observed awkwardness with nested discriminators inside arrays — design decision: only top-level discriminators required; nested items must define their own discriminator explicitly.

2026-02-03: Diego implemented initial zodify flag (--emit-zod). Output artifacts: .d.ts, .zod.ts, .jsonschema.json. Ran into JSON-Schema limitation mapping optional/nullable union branches. Trade-off: emit 'oneOf' with discriminatorMapping and include explicit 'nullable' variants for nullability.

2026-02-10: Review by Lina: asked for progressive parsing hooks: suggestions to return { partial: Partial<T>, stable?: boolean, errors?: string[] }. We iterated and reduced shape to (partial: Partial<T>, complete: boolean, diagnostics: string[]).

2026-02-18: Integration with streaming runtime: added 'progressiveKV' cache hint to help incremental parser keep state across tokens. Prototype shows successful rehydration across three chunk boundaries for examples/variant-chat session.
2026-02-26: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ts-sdk/pull/1423 — includes emitter, zodify, jsonschema, and streaming helpers. Unit tests added for five canonical contract fixtures.

2026-03-03: Feedback from Marco: prefer generator API to be idempotent and hermetic for CI—emitter should embed a generation-hash header to detect drift. Action: add header and update CI job to fail on mismatches.
2026-03-05: Security team note: JSON-Schema artifacts may contain PII examples in fixtures. We added scrub step in emitter that strips example values unless --include-examples is set.
implementation_steps: Design: finalize discriminator naming and nested-discriminator policy
Emitter: add TypeScript AST pipeline to produce union types and variant interfaces
Zod generator: produce zod schemas mirroring types (with progressive parse helper functions)
JSON-Schema export: map zod -> JSON-Schema carefully handling oneOf + discriminatorMapping
Streaming parser: build decodeIncremental API and state machine to reassemble partials
CI: add contract validation job and generation-hash check
Rollout: feature flag in SDK release and opt-in CLI flag --emit-polymorphix
risks: Edge cases: model-generated discriminator collisions, deeply nested polymorphism complexity, and JSON-Schema expressiveness mismatch. Risk of increased bundle size from zod schemas—we will provide opt-in flag and tree-shakeable outputs.
open_questions: Should emitter canonicalize discriminator values (lowercase) or preserve model-provided casing?
Do we provide runtime fallback that attempts to infer variant from shape if discriminator missing? (costs complexity)
What compatibility guarantees do we promise for generated JSON-Schema between minor SDK releases?
